summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — BAB.L +7%, CCC.L +5%, FRES.L +3%, EDV.L +3%, STMPA.PA +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (KGF.L -4%, BNR.DE -4%, HWDN.L -3%, BNZL.L -3%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: BAB.L (+7.43%) — Babcock Canada disclosed a ~$1.1bn six-year extension of the Victoria-class submarine in-service support contract (announced 20 Jul), layering on ongoing buyback/FY26-beat momentum. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: Babcock is a UK defence/gov-services mid-cap, likely screened out by a defense-sector exclusion list or an index-membership filter that omits contract-news-driven names like this.

top_movers.catalyst: No company news; tracked a ~5% spot silver rebound ($58→$59/oz) on eased US-Iran tension/rate-hike fears — Fresnillo is the world's largest silver miner, a high-beta proxy for the metal.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — falls in the UK-listed metals/mining large-cap bucket, a commodity-linked equity category the uk-eu universes don't currently cover, so the move was never seen regardless of filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a precious-metals miner basket (FRES.L, HOC.L, etc.) to the uk-eu universe with a rule that flags names when the underlying spot metal (XAG/XAU) moves >3% intraday.
